198	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
199	    """JSON booleans are ints in Python; checkpoints treat them as wrong."""
200	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
201	
202	
203	def _as_cell(value: object, description: str) -> Position:
204	    """Validate a user supplied coordinate as a two-integer pair."""
205	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
206	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
207	    if len(value) != 2:
208	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
209	    if not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value):
210	        raise ValueError(f"{description} coordinates must be integers, not booleans or other types")
211	    return value[0], value[1]
212	
213	
214	def _as_pair(value: object, description: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
215	    if (
216	        not isinstance(value, list)
217	        or len(value) != 2
218	        or not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value)
219	    ):
220	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
221	    return value[0], value[1]
222	
223	
224	def _task_route_waypoints(origin: Position, task: Task) -> list[Position]:
225	    """Required remaining visit points after *origin* for *task*.
226	
227	    The same pickup/delivery rule is used by first-time assignment, rerouting
228	    after map changes (and the recovery/sidestep planning that shares it) and
229	    checkpoint validation, so the requirement lives in exactly one place:
230	
231	    * Goods not yet collected: the route must still reach the pickup and then
232	      the dropoff. Standing exactly on the pickup makes the pickup leg empty --
233	      the leg contributes no waypoint -- but planning never collects or
234	      completes anything by itself.
235	    * Goods already collected: the robot routes straight to the dropoff, even
236	      when the old pickup cell was closed afterwards; it is never sent back.
237	
238	    When *origin*, pickup and dropoff coincide the list is empty, which
239	    describes a feasible zero-step route and must not be confused with an
240	    unreachable one.
241	    """
242	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
243	    if not task.picked_up and origin != task.pickup:
244	        waypoints.append(task.pickup)
245	    last = waypoints[-1] if waypoints else origin
246	    if task.dropoff != last:
247	        waypoints.append(task.dropoff)
248	    return waypoints
249	
250	
251	def _plan_task_route(
252	    grid: GridMap, origin: Position, task: Task
253	) -> list[Position] | None:
254	    """Shortest feasible route through the task's required waypoints.
255	
256	    The returned list holds the cells after *origin* only, concatenating the
257	    deterministic shortest legs between consecutive required points. It is
258	    ``None`` when any required point cannot be reached, and an empty list for a
259	    feasible route with zero steps (origin already at the only destination).
260	    """
261	    route: list[Position] = []
262	    current = origin
263	    for waypoint in _task_route_waypoints(origin, task):
264	        try:
265	            leg = shortest_path(grid, current, waypoint)
266	        except ValueError:
267	            return None
268	        route.extend(leg)
269	        current = waypoint
270	    return route

273	class FleetSimulator:
274	    def __init__(self, grid: GridMap, robots: list[Robot], tasks: list[Task]) -> None:
275	        self.grid = grid
276	        # The map as built before any runtime edit; map-change history is
277	        # replayed against this baseline.
278	        self.base_grid = grid
279	        self.robots = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
280	        self.tasks = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
281	        self.tick = 0
282	        self.replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
283	        self.map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
284	        self._map_sequence = 0
285	        self.paused_tasks: set[str] = set()
286	        # Consecutive per-robot waits caused purely by other robots:
287	        # robot_id -> {"blocked_by": [robot_id, ...], "ticks": int}.
288	        self._traffic_waits: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
289	        positions = [robot.position for robot in robots]
290	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
291	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
292	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):
293	            raise ValueError("robot starts outside traversable map space")
294	        self._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
295	        # Accepted routes share one internal shape regardless of how the caller
296	        # spelled them: a mutable list of tuple cells. The normalized copies are
297	        # committed only after every robot passed validation, so a rejection
298	        # (even one buried in a later robot's route) never touches the caller's
299	        # objects. See :meth:`_normalize_initial_routes`.
300	        normalized_routes = self._normalize_initial_routes(grid, robots)
301	        for robot, route in zip(robots, normalized_routes):
302	            robot.route = route
303	
304	    @staticmethod
305	    def _validate_task_ownership(robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]) -> None:
306	        """Reject impossible initial bindings between robots and tasks.
307	
308	        The very same mutual-ownership requirement backs direct construction
309	        and checkpoint loading, so it lives in exactly one place. The binding
310	        only governs work still in progress:
311	
312	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
313	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
314	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
315	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
316	          collected additionally must have an owner.
317	        * A robot can therefore never be claimed by two unfinished tasks: the
318	          second task's owner points at a robot that executes another task.
319	
320	        Completed tasks only keep *historical* ownership: their recorded
321	        ``assigned_robot`` is not required to be idle or to name them back, so
322	        a robot that already finished one task may be idle or busy with a new
323	        one. Unassigned, not-yet-collected tasks simply wait -- even when no
324	        robot can reach them -- and are not an ownership error. Nothing here
325	        rewrites a binding or drops a task; an inconsistent input is rejected
326	        as a whole with a :class:`ValueError` naming the conflicting robot or
327	        task, leaving the caller's objects untouched.
328	        """
329	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
330	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
331	        for robot in robots:
332	            if robot.task_id is None:
333	                continue
334	            task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
335	            if task is None:
336	                raise ValueError(
337	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task "
338	                    f"{robot.task_id!r}"
339	                )
340	            if task.completed:
341	                raise ValueError(
342	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
343	                    "that is already completed"
344	                )
345	            if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
346	                raise ValueError(
347	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
348	                    f"but the task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
349	                )
350	        for task in tasks:
351	            # Completed tasks retain historical ownership; their robots are
352	            # free to take new work, so the mutual binding only holds while a
353	            # task is still in progress.
354	            if task.completed:
355	                continue
356	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
357	                raise ValueError(
358	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
359	                )
360	            if task.assigned_robot is not None:
361	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
362	                if owner is None:
363	                    raise ValueError(
364	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
365	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
366	                    )
367	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
368	                    raise ValueError(
369	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} "
370	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
371	                    )
372	
373	    @staticmethod
374	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
375	        grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]
376	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
377	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
378	
379	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound: a route carries no current
380	        cell, so a non-empty route must begin with an orthogonal neighbour of
381	        the robot's position and every later waypoint must be one orthogonal
382	        step from the previous one. Diagonal moves, multi-cell jumps, two
383	        identical consecutive waypoints and a first waypoint equal to the
384	        current cell are all rejected, and every waypoint must lie inside the
385	        map and outside its obstacles. The outer route may be a list or tuple
386	        and each waypoint may itself be a list or tuple of two plain integers
387	        -- booleans are not integers here, and wrong lengths or element types
388	        raise :class:`ValueError` instead of leaking unpacking or hashing
389	        failures. The forms may be mixed freely; only the coordinate order
390	        matters, not the container types.
391	
392	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
393	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
394	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
395	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
396	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
397	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
398	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
399	
400	        The check is read-only -- normalization happens on fresh lists, and
401	        the caller commits them itself only once every robot has passed, so a
402	        rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a later robot or at
403	        the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders or otherwise
404	        modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. Checkpoint loading
405	        keeps its own, stricter validation that also covers the task
406	        pickup/dropoff rules.
407	        """
408	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
409	        for robot in robots:
410	            route = robot.route
411	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
412	                raise ValueError(
413	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
414	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
415	                )
416	            waypoints: list[Position] = []
417	            previous = robot.position
418	            for index, cell in enumerate(route):
419	                waypoint = _as_cell(
420	                    cell, f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route waypoint {index}"
421	                )
422	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
423	                    raise ValueError(
424	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route waypoint {index} "
425	                        f"{list(waypoint)} is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
426	                    )
427	                if index == 0 and waypoint == previous:
428	                    raise ValueError(
429	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route waypoint 0 "
430	                        f"{list(waypoint)} is the robot's current cell; the "
431	                        "remaining route must start with the next cell"
432	                    )
433	                if waypoint == previous:
434	                    raise ValueError(
435	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route repeats cell "
436	                        f"{list(waypoint)} at consecutive waypoints "
437	                        f"{index - 1} and {index}"
438	                    )
439	                if (
440	                    abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0])
441	                    + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1])
442	                    != 1
443	                ):
444	                    if index == 0:
445	                        segment = (
446	                            f"from its current position {list(previous)} to "
447	                            f"route waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)}"
448	                        )
449	                    else:
450	                        segment = (
451	                            f"from route waypoint {index - 1} {list(previous)} "
452	                            f"to waypoint {index} {list(waypoint)}"
453	                        )
454	                    raise ValueError(
455	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently "
456	                        f"{segment}: every step must move one orthogonal cell"
457	                    )
458	                waypoints.append(waypoint)
459	                previous = waypoint
460	            normalized.append(waypoints)
461	        return normalized

464	    # Dynamic map edits
465	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

467	    def modify_obstacles(
468	        self,
469	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
470	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
471	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
472	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
473	
474	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
475	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
476	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
477	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
478	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
479	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
480	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
481	
482	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
483	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
484	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
485	        distance is accumulated.
486	        """
487	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
488	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
489	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
490	        if conflict:
491	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
492	            raise ValueError(
493	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
494	            )
495	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
496	        for cell in add_cells:
497	            if cell in occupied:
498	                raise ValueError(
499	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
500	                )
501	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
502	
503	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
504	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
505	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
506	        seen: set[Position] = set()
507	        ordered: list[Position] = []
508	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
509	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
510	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
511	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
512	            if position in seen:
513	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
514	                continue
515	            seen.add(position)
516	            ordered.append(position)
517	        return ordered
518	
519	    def _apply_map_change(
520	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
521	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
522	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
523	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
524	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
525	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
526	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
527	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
528	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
529	
530	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
531	        # known to change the map.
532	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
533	        self._map_sequence += 1
534	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
535	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
536	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
537	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
538	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
539	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
540	
541	    def _map_change_record(
542	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
543	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
544	        return {
545	            "type": "map_change",
546	            "tick": self.tick,
547	            "sequence": sequence,
548	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
549	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
550	        }

552	    def _plan_route(
553	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
554	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
555	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
556	
557	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
558	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
559	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
560	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
561	        """
562	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
563	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)
564	
565	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
566	        for task in self.tasks.values():
567	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
568	                continue
569	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
570	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
571	                continue
572	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
573	            if route is None:
574	                robot.route = []
575	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
576	            else:
577	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
578	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
579	                robot.route = route
580	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
581	
582	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
583	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
584	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
585	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
586	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
587	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
588	                continue
589	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
590	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
591	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
592	                continue
593	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
594	            if route is None:
595	                robot.route = []
596	                continue
597	            robot.route = route
598	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
599	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

603	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
604	
605	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
606	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
607	        cells: set[Position] = set()
608	        for robot in self.robots.values():
609	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
610	                cells.update(robot.route)
611	        return cells
612	
613	    def _safe_side_cells(
614	        self,
615	        robot: Robot,
616	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
617	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
618	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
619	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
620	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
621	
622	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
623	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
624	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
625	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
626	
627	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
628	          skips anything else),
629	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
630	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
631	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
632	          route is excluded), and
633	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
634	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
635	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
636	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
637	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
638	
639	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
640	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
641	        """
642	        blocked = set(forbidden)
643	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
644	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
645	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
646	                continue
647	            yield cell
648	
649	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
650	        self,
651	        blocker: Robot,
652	        requester: Robot,
653	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
654	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
655	    ) -> Position | None:
656	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
657	
658	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
659	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
660	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
661	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
662	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
663	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
664	        """
665	        return next(
666	            self._safe_side_cells(
667	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
668	            ),
669	            None,
670	        )
671	
672	    def _self_sidestep(
673	        self,
674	        robot: Robot,
675	        task: Task | None,
676	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
677	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
678	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
679	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
680	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
681	
682	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
683	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
684	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
685	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
686	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
687	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
688	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
689	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
690	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
691	        """
692	        if task is None or task.completed:
693	            return None
694	        destination = robot.route[0]
695	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
696	        if blocker_id is None:
697	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
698	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
699	        best_length = 0
700	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
701	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
702	        # that order as the tie break.
703	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
704	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
705	            if route is None:
706	                continue
707	            if (
708	                blocker_id is not None
709	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
710	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
711	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
712	                )
713	            ):
714	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
715	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
716	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
717	                continue
718	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
719	                best = (cell, route)
720	                best_length = len(route)
721	        return best
722	
723	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
724	        self,
725	        robot: Robot,
726	        side: Position,
727	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
728	        blocker_id: str,
729	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
730	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
731	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
732	    ) -> bool:
733	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
734	
735	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
736	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
737	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
738	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
739	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
740	        never rejected here.
741	        """
742	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
743	            return False
744	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
745	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
746	            return False
747	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
748	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
749	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
750	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
751	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
752	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
753	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
754	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
755	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
756	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
757	        return not self._can_vacate(
758	            blocker,
759	            robot,
760	            hyp_occupied,
761	            reserved,
762	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
763	            blocked_path,
764	        )
765	
766	    def _can_vacate(
767	        self,
768	        blocker: Robot,
769	        requester: Robot,
770	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
771	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
772	        checking: frozenset[str],
773	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
774	    ) -> bool:
775	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
776	
777	        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
778	        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
779	        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
780	        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
781	        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
782	        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
783	        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots whose leave check
784	        is already on the call stack, so a cyclic dependency (a head-on
785	        deadlock, or the requester itself) is not assumed resolvable.
786	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
787	        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
788	        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
789	        the blocker's own route does).
790	        """
791	        if blocker.robot_id in checking:
792	            return False
793	        task = self.tasks[blocker.task_id] if blocker.task_id is not None else None
794	        if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
795	            return False
796	        if not blocker.route:
797	            if task is not None:
798	                # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this
799	                # tick; it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
800	                return False
801	            # A parked robot (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
802	            # yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; it does
803	            # so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
804	            # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
805	            # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
806	            # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
807	            side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, requester, occupied, reserved)
808	            return side is not None and side not in blocked_path
809	        ahead = blocker.route[0]
810	        if (
811	            self.grid.traversable(ahead)
812	            and ahead not in occupied
813	            and ahead not in reserved
814	        ):
815	            return True
816	        occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
817	        if (
818	            occupant_id is not None
819	            and occupant_id != blocker.robot_id
820	            and occupant_id not in checking
821	        ):
822	            # The blocker could follow the robot ahead once that robot
823	            # vacates its cell this same tick.
824	            if self._can_vacate(
825	                self.robots[occupant_id],
826	                requester,
827	                occupied,
828	                reserved,
829	                checking | {blocker.robot_id},
830	                blocked_path,
831	            ):
832	                return True
833	        if task is None:
834	            # A taskless robot that still drives a remaining route never
835	            # sidesteps off it -- not even to unblock a requester -- so a side
836	            # cell cannot count as a way out for it.
837	            return False
838	        # Otherwise the task-bound blocker might sidestep onto a free side
839	        # cell itself, but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has
840	        # to use -- parking there only moves the blockage.
841	        for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
842	            blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
843	        ):
844	            if self._plan_route(blocker, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
845	                return True
846	        return False
847	
848	    def _update_traffic_waits(
849	        self,
850	        waited: dict[str, str],
851	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
852	    ) -> None:
853	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
854	
855	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
856	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
857	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
858	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
859	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
860	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
861	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
862	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
863	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
864	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
865	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
866	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
867	        """
868	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
869	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
870	        for robot_id in waited:
871	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
872	                continue
873	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
874	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
875	                continue
876	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
877	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
878	                continue
879	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
880	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
881	                continue
882	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
883	            if entry is None:
884	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
885	            else:
886	                surviving[robot_id] = {
887	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
888	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
889	                }
890	        self._traffic_waits = surviving
891	
892	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
893	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
894	
895	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
896	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
897	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
898	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
899	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
900	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
901	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
902	        """
903	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
904	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
905	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
906	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
907	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
908	                continue
909	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
910	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
911	
912	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
913	        return [
914	            {
915	                "robot_id": robot_id,
916	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
917	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
918	            }
919	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
920	        ]

926	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
927	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest idle robot using stable tie breaks."""
928	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
929	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
930	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
931	            for robot in self.robots.values():
932	                if not robot.idle:
933	                    continue
934	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
935	                if route is None:
936	                    continue
937	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
938	            if not choices:
939	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
940	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
941	                continue
942	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
943	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
944	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
945	            robot.route = route
946	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
947	
948	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
949	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
950	        for robot in self.robots.values():
951	            if robot.task_id is None:
952	                continue
953	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
954	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
955	                task.picked_up = True
956	
957	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
958	        self._confirm_pickups()
959	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
960	        self.assign_tasks()
961	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
962	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
963	        self._confirm_pickups()
964	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
965	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
966	        moved: list[str] = []
967	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
968	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
969	
970	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
971	            del occupied[robot.position]
972	            robot.position = destination
973	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
974	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
975	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
976	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
977	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
978	
979	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
980	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
981	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
982	                continue
983	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
984	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
985	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
986	                continue
987	            if not robot.route:
988	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
989	                continue
990	            destination = robot.route[0]
991	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
992	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
993	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
994	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
995	                    if route is None:
996	                        robot.route = []
997	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
998	                    else:
999	                        robot.route = route
1000	                continue
1001	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
1002	            if blocker_id is None:
1003	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
1004	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
1005	                relocate(robot, destination)
1006	                robot.route.pop(0)
1007	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1008	                continue
1009	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
1010	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
1011	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
1012	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:
1013	                if blocker.task_id is None and not blocker.route:
1014	                    # Truly parked blocker: no bound task and no remaining
1015	                    # route. Ask it to yield onto a free side cell, then take
1016	                    # over the cell it vacated. A taskless robot that still has
1017	                    # a remaining route is not parked: it drives that route
1018	                    # cell by cell like any other moving robot and is never
1019	                    # pushed off it for a requester.
1020	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
1021	                    if side is not None:
1022	                        relocate(blocker, side)
1023	                        relocate(robot, destination)
1024	                        robot.route.pop(0)
1025	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1026	                        continue
1027	                if blocker.route:
1028	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
1029	                    if (
1030	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
1031	                        and ahead not in occupied
1032	                        and ahead not in reserved
1033	                    ):
1034	                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
1035	                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
1036	                        blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
1037	                        continue
1038	            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
1039	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
1040	            side = self._self_sidestep(
1041	                robot, task, occupied, reserved, frozenset(moved_ids)
1042	            )
1043	            if side is not None:
1044	                cell, route = side
1045	                relocate(robot, cell)
1046	                robot.route = route
1047	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1048	                continue
1049	            blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
1050	        self._update_traffic_waits(blocked_by, frozenset(moved_ids))
1051	        self.tick += 1
1052	        event: dict[str, object] = {
1053	            "type": "tick",
1054	            "tick": self.tick,
1055	            "moved": moved,
1056	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
1057	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
1058	        }
1059	        self.replay.append(event)
1060	        return event

1062	    def _finish_if_arrived(self, robot: Robot) -> None:
1063	        if robot.task_id is None:
1064	            return
1065	        task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
1066	        if task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1067	            return
1068	        if robot.position == task.pickup:
1069	            task.picked_up = True
1070	        if task.picked_up and robot.position == task.dropoff and not robot.route:
1071	            task.completed = True
1072	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
1073	            robot.task_id = None

1115	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
1116	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
1117	
1118	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
1119	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
1120	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
1121	        raise :class:`OSError`.
1122	        """
1123	        document = {
1124	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
1125	            "grid": {
1126	                "width": self.grid.width,
1127	                "height": self.grid.height,
1128	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
1129	            },
1130	            "base_grid": {
1131	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
1132	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
1133	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
1134	            },
1135	            "tick": self.tick,
1136	            "robots": [
1137	                {
1138	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
1139	                    "position": list(robot.position),
1140	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
1141	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
1142	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
1143	                }
1144	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
1145	            ],
1146	            "tasks": [
1147	                {
1148	                    "task_id": task.task_id,
1149	                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
1150	                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
1151	                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
1152	                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
1153	                    "completed": task.completed,
1154	                }
1155	                for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)
1156	            ],
1157	            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
1158	            "map_changes": copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes),
1159	            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
1160	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
1161	        }
1162	        payload = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
1163	
1164	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))) or os.curdir
1165	        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
1166	        try:
1167	            handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
1168	            try:
1169	                handle.write(payload)
1170	                handle.flush()
1171	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
1172	            finally:
1173	                handle.close()
1174	            os.replace(tmp_name, path)
1175	            self._fsync_directory(directory)
1176	        except BaseException:
1177	            # After a successful replace the temp name is already gone.
1178	            try:
1179	                os.unlink(tmp_name)
1180	            except OSError:
1181	                pass
1182	            raise

1184	    @staticmethod

1186	        try:
1187	            dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
1188	        except OSError:
1189	            return
1190	        try:
1191	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
1192	        except OSError:
1193	            pass
1194	        finally:
1195	            os.close(dir_fd)

1198	    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FleetSimulator:
1199	        """Load an independent simulator instance from *path*.
1200	
1201	        The returned simulator shares no mutable state with the file or any
1202	        other loaded instance. Invalid checkpoint content raises
1203	        :class:`ValueError` explaining the reason; read/permission failures
1204	        propagate as :class:`OSError`.
1205	        """
1206	        try:
1207	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
1208	                text = handle.read()

1210	            raise
1211	        try:
1212	            data = json.loads(text)

1217	    @classmethod
1218	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
1219	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
1220	            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")
1221	
1222	        version = data.get("version")
1223	        if not _is_int(version):
1224	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
1225	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
1226	            raise ValueError(
1227	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
1228	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
1229	            )
1230	
1231	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
1232	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
1233	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
1234	
1235	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1236	        paused: set[str] = set()
1237	        if version == 1:
1238	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
1239	            base_grid = grid
1240	        else:
1241	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
1242	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
1243	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
1244	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
1245	            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
1246	                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")
1247	            cls._validate_map_history(base_grid, grid, map_changes)
1248	
1249	        robots: list[Robot] = []
1250	        for record in robot_records:
1251	            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
1252	            if not grid.traversable(position):
1253	                raise ValueError(
1254	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
1255	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
1256	                )
1257	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
1258	            previous = position
1259	            for index, cell in enumerate(record["route"]):
1260	                waypoint = _as_pair(
1261	                    cell, f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {index}"
1262	                )
1263	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
1264	                    raise ValueError(
1265	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
1266	                        "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
1267	                    )
1268	                if abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0]) + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1]) != 1:
1269	                    raise ValueError(
1270	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
1271	                        f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
1272	                    )
1273	                route.append(waypoint)
1274	                previous = waypoint
1275	            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
1276	            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
1277	                raise ValueError(
1278	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
1279	                    "non-negative integer"
1280	                )
1281	            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))
1282	
1283	        tasks: list[Task] = []
1284	        for record in task_records:
1285	            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
1286	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
1287	            tasks.append(
1288	                Task(
1289	                    record["task_id"],
1290	                    pickup,
1291	                    dropoff,
1292	                    record["assigned_robot"],
1293	                    record["picked_up"],
1294	                    record["completed"],
1295	                )
1296	            )
1297	
1298	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
1299	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
1300	
1301	        # Ownership is judged with the exact rules direct construction uses:
1302	        # mutual bindings for work in progress, historical owners for finished
1303	        # tasks, and a collected task that may never lack its carrier.
1304	        cls._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
1305	        for task in tasks:
1306	            if task.completed and not task.picked_up:
1307	                raise ValueError(
1308	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is completed but never picked up"
1309	                )
1310	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
1311	                # Direct construction never sees a finished task without a
1312	                # historical owner because it cannot create completion itself,
1313	                # but a checkpoint document can spell one, and the running
1314	                # simulator only ever saves picked-up tasks with a carrier.
1315	                raise ValueError(
1316	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
1317	                )
1318	
1319	        cls._validate_paused_state(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id, grid)
1320	        cls._validate_active_task_routes(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id)
1321	        traffic_waits = cls._load_traffic_waits(data, robot_by_id)
1322	
1323	        replay_change_frames = cls._replay_map_change_frames(replay)
1324	        if replay_change_frames != map_changes:

1327	        simulator = cls(grid, robots, tasks)
1328	        simulator.base_grid = base_grid
1329	        simulator.tick = tick
1330	        simulator.replay = copy.deepcopy(replay)
1331	        simulator.map_changes = copy.deepcopy(map_changes)
1332	        simulator._map_sequence = len(map_changes)
1333	        simulator.paused_tasks = set(paused)
1334	        simulator._traffic_waits = traffic_waits

1338	        # map.
1339	        cls._validate_replay_positions(replay, tick, robot_by_id, base_grid, map_changes)
